# Part III. Heuristics, Biases, and Choice Across Time {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

A bounded mind needs shortcuts. The important question is not whether a judgment was fast, but whether the cue and rule fit the environment. This part moves from the two-mode framework to heuristics, probability, bias, framing, priming, and cognitive ease, then brings those mechanisms together in choices across time.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What easier question did the mind answer?
- Is the shortcut adapted to this environment?
- What denominator, reference class, or comparison is missing?
- What would make a slow inspection worth its cost?
- What besides pure time preference makes a delayed outcome lose weight?
